title: Direct Field Modification of Colleague (Porous Encapsulation)
pattern: A struct directly reads and modifies the public, mutable field of an associated struct rather than telling it to perform the action.
why_bad: It violates basic encapsulation ("Tell, Don't Ask"). If the logic for oil consumption changes (e.g., consumption rate varies with RPM), the caller (`Car`) must change instead of the `Engine`.
detection: Code outside of struct `T` modifying a field of `T` directly using assignment operators.
counterexample: Simple configuration structs or pure "data holders" (structs with no behavior/methods) designed purely as plain-old-data DTOs.
source: Martin Fowler, *Refactoring* (1999), Chapter 3 ("Inappropriate Intimacy"); Steve McConnell, *Code Complete* (2004), Chapter 5 ("Design in Construction").
